verdicts.note: Watch-out about truncation used a confusing 9830.9 example; reworded.
Told learner to 'clip' before clipping is taught; now just says check the range.
Claimed x^2 is computed exactly; it is computed directly with full relative accuracy.
Ref pointed to Python Tutorial ch. 15, which does not cover math.isclose; now cites math.isclose docs (PEP 485).
Gradient and loss were never taught; added a one-sentence gloss.
Said 16 guard bits allow billions of worst-case products; correct figure is 131,071.
FIR filter and tap were used undefined; defined in the prompt.
FIR filters mentioned without explanation; added a short gloss.
Implied only a 32-bit sum gets dual-16 MAC; M4 SMLALD does it with a 64-bit sum. Rewrote the other side around cores without a 64-bit MAC (Cortex-M0), and the SMLAL cost note.

summary.notes: All C and Python snippets compiled and run (sanitizers clean); Q15/Q7, float32 encodings, FP16/BF16 limits, FMA, tie and accumulator numbers recomputed. Arm instruction facts (SSAT/USAT M3+M4, QADD M4 only, no saturation on M0) and CMSIS q15 FIR 64-bit vs fast 32-bit accumulator consistent with my knowledge; Yiu section numbers and Horowitz figures not independently re-verified.
